proof.text: By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality], each chosen small strict-local ring is local and strictly henselian, and its structural morphism [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map] sends the closed point to the given geometric point. Every point of the spectrum of a local ring generalizes its closed point. Continuity and stability of open sets under generalization therefore put the whole image of the structural map in each prescribed affine open. The open-immersion lifting property gives its factorization, and [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives the ring maps a and b.

proof.text: Use the structural square for the canonical pointed map from [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]. For any a and b satisfying the displayed factorizations, compose Spec(h) followed by Spec(a), and Spec(b) followed by Spec(f), with the open immersion i_U. Both composites equal j_T followed by g, by the structural square, the factorization equations and the chart equation. Cancel the monomorphism i_U and apply the faithful spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] to obtain h.comp a = b.comp f. Thus h is an A-algebra map for the structures a and b.comp f.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-small-strict-henselization-ind-etale] with its parameters $(S,s,R,i,A,e,a)$ instantiated by $(S,s,A,i_U,H_S,\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}H_S},a)$. Here $S_{(s)}=\operatorname{Spec}H_S$ is precisely the small representative model fixed in the item. The chart contains the image of $s$, $i_U$ is an affine open immersion, and the required equation is $i_U\circ\operatorname{Spec}a=j_S\circ\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}H_S}$, which is Step 1. Thus $a$ makes $H_S$ ind-etale over $A$. Apply the same statement with parameters $(T,t,B,i_V,H_T,\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}H_T},b)$; the chart contains the image of $t$ and its structural-map equation is $i_V\circ\operatorname{Spec}b=j_T\circ\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}H_T}$, again Step 1. Both sides in the first application map $\operatorname{Spec}H_S$ to $S$, and in the second map $\operatorname{Spec}H_T$ to $T$. Thus $b$ makes $H_T$ ind-etale over $B$. These are applications to the chosen small colimits, with no identification with a different strict-henselization construction and no extra condition on either chart ring.

proof.text: The hypothesis gives that $f:A\to B$ is ind-etale, and Step 3 gives that $b:B\to H_T$ is ind-etale. Composition stability in [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] therefore gives that $b\circ f:A\to H_T$ is ind-etale. Thus $H_S$ and $H_T$ are both ind-etale $A$-algebras for exactly the structures $a$ and $b\circ f$.

Apply relative permanence in [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] to the A-algebra map h of Step 2 between the two ind-etale A-algebras of Steps 3 and 4. This gives ind-etaleness of h. The canonical ULift definition is equivalent to ordinary ind-etaleness here because every ring is in universe u: transport along ULift.ringEquiv using invariance under ring isomorphisms. For locality, identify the pointed residue formula of clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality] with canonical point evaluation: their spectrum maps have the same composites with every limit projection of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], so limit extensionality and spectrum faithfulness identify them. This formula is local, being a composite of the local residue map, the residue isomorphism, and a field embedding. The defining pointed equation of the canonical map now says evaluation_S = evaluation_T.comp h. Locality of this composite implies locality of h. Clause (1) already supplied strict henselianity, and the defining structural square supplies the final equality.

title: The canonical strict-local ring comparison is ind-etale on an ind-etale chart
statement: Let $u:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and put $s=u\circ t$, using the same algebraically closed field $\Omega$. Suppose there are affine open subschemes $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset T$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion] containing the images of $t$ and $s$, with $u(V)\subset U$, such that the induced homomorphism $f:A\to B$ is ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Write $H_S=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,s}$, $H_T=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{T,t}$ for the chosen small pointed-neighbourhood colimits [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and $j_S:\operatorname{Spec}H_S\to S$, $j_T:\operatorname{Spec}H_T\to T$ for their structural morphisms [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Let $h:H_S\to H_T$ be the canonical local homomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]. Then $j_S$ and $j_T$ factor through $U$ and $V$, respectively. If $a:A\to H_S$ and $b:B\to H_T$ are the ring homomorphisms of these factorizations, then $h\circ a=b\circ f$, and $a$, $b$, $b\circ f$, and $h$ are ind-etale. In particular, $h$ is a local homomorphism of strictly henselian local rings [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] satisfying $j_S\circ\operatorname{Spec}h=u\circ j_T$. No local ind-etaleness away from these chosen charts is required.
